extracted.intended_audience: researchers, principal investigators, and institutions interested in applying for or participating in DOE Energy Frontier Research Centers (EFRC) funding
extracted.subtask_description: Program-level criteria and expectations for Energy Frontier Research Centers: what centers are expected to do, how they are structured, topical focus areas, funding cadence, and workforce/training goals for applicants and participating institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidisciplinary, multi-institutional teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers bring together creative, multidisciplinary, and multi-institutional teams of scientific researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFRCs are expected to assemble teams across disciplines and institutions to leverage diverse expertise; this collaborative structure is a defining feature of the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the toughest grand scientific challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers are charged to address the toughest grand scientific challenges at the forefront of fundamental energy science research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals/centers should target high‑impact, frontier problems in fundamental energy science rather than incremental or narrowly scoped topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target both discovery science and use‑inspired basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: These centers provide the foundation for collaborative efforts that target both discovery science and use-inspired basic research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful centers should balance fundamental discovery with research that is motivated by potential energy-relevant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align with priority research directions identified by the community
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers aim to address priority research directions and opportunities identified by the scientific community in a series of BES workshop and roundtable reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should reference and align with community-identified priorities from BES workshops/roundtables to demonstrate responsiveness to field-wide needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit advanced characterization, modeling, and manipulation tools across scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers take full advantage of powerful new tools for characterizing, understanding, modeling, and manipulating matter from atomic to macroscopic length scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFRC activities should leverage state-of-the-art instrumentation, modeling, and multiscale approaches; proposals should describe how such tools will be integrated to achieve center goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train the next-generation scientific workforce
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers train the next-generation scientific workforce by attracting talented students and postdoctoral researchers interested in energy science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workforce development—mentoring, training opportunities, recruitment of students/postdocs—should be an explicit element of center plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding cadence and award duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Biennial funding opportunities for 4-year awards started in 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should plan projects and budgets around 4‑year award periods and solicitations issued approximately every two years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted competitions and topical focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasional targeted competitions focus on specific areas (example: 2024 targeted competition in advanced manufacturing, including polymers and co-design of materials and processes, and environmental management of nuclear waste tanks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFRC solicitations may specify topic areas for that competition; applicants should respond to any targeted topics and demonstrate relevance to the solicitation’s stated focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centres should support DOE initiatives across key fundamental energy science areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Each center has its own unique mission that supports the Department of Energy’s initiatives in advancing basic energy research across the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFRCs are expected to complement DOE priorities and together cover areas such as advanced manufacturing, energy storage, environmental management, hydrogen, microelectronics, nuclear, quantum information science, separations, solar, and the subsurface; proposals should articulate how the center’s mission supports DOE goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a foundation for collaborative, high-impact research
rubrics_metrics.description: These centers provide the foundation for collaborative efforts that target priority research directions and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFRCs are intended to catalyze sustained, large-scale collaborations and deliverable advances in fundamental knowledge that underpin energy technologies; proposals should demonstrate mechanisms for collaboration, deliverables, and impact.
